title: Edge-sliced Prefill Orchestrator with KV demultiplexing and decode handshake refactor
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: We see persistent tail latency bimodality on mixed interactive workloads where long prefill windows for some sessions block kernel reuse and trigger KV cache thrashing. Prior prefilling approaches either prefill large contiguous windows (high KV churn) or micro-chunk aggressively (excess kernel dispatch overhead). Motivation: reduce end-to-end tail latency without regressing throughput and keep per-tenant KV coherence across overlapping prefill/decodes. This PR introduces the Edge-sliced Prefill Orchestrator: a middle-ground that slices prefill work into edge-aligned segments that 1) align with kernel-friendly shapes, 2) expose overlap points for decode to start early, and 3) feed an updated KV demultiplexer to avoid cross-session cache eviction. Key changes (high level): - runtime/prefill/orchestrator.cpp: new orchestrator that allocates "edge slices" based on per-model token shape histograms and current KV pressure. Slices prefer ends of sequences (edges) first to maximize early decode overlap. - runtime/scheduler/slice_allocator.cc: slice-aware resource allocator that schedules slices with priority buckets (hot-slices, neutral, background) and integrates with the pre-existing token-bucket admission controller. - runtime/kv/cache_demux.cc & runtime/kv/cache_demux.h: KV demultiplexer that shards KV cache entries by affinity vectors (tenant, model-variant, slice-hash) and includes soft-eviction hints to the scheduler. - runtime/kernels/kernel_hint.h & user-facing hints: a small interface so orchestrator can pass kernel-friendly shapes (seq_len, microbatch) and preferred compute backend (f16/quantized path). - runtime/decode/handshake_refactor.{cc,h}: decouple the previous monolithic handshake into two phases: RSVP (locks necessary KV pages) and START_DECODE (kick off decode kernels as slices arrive). This reduces blocked prefill time and makes decode start opportunistically. - tests/perf/prefill_overlap_bench.py: new harness that reproduces mixed interactive workload and measures tail P50/P95/P99 end-to-end latency and per-token cost. - docs/architecture/prefill-edge-slicing.md: design doc and rollout notes. Commits: - Add edge-sliced orchestrator and slice allocator (Maya Chen) - Implement KV demultiplexer and eviction hints (Maya Chen) - Kernel hint API and small kernel-side consumer stub (Tom Becker) - Refactor decode handshake into RSVP/START_DECODE phases (Priya Natarajan) - Add perf harness, CI benchmarks, and docs (Maya Chen) Implementation notes: - The orchestrator samples model sequence-length distributions from recent request histograms to pick slice boundaries that are likely to be kernel-friendly (powers-of-two or multiples of 16 where kernels are optimized). - Edge-first slicing: for most user prompts the tail tokens are more latency-sensitive; we create small slices at the edges (<=16 tokens) and schedule them at higher priority so decode can begin earlier while the rest of the prefill continues. - KV demultiplexing: instead of a global LRU causing eviction across unrelated traffic, demux shards by affinity vectors and maintains per-shard age metrics. The scheduler consults these metrics to avoid scheduling slices that would immediately thrash a hot shard. - Handshake refactor: RSVP acquires soft locks on KV pages and returns immediately if decode can start; START_DECODE is idempotent and will no-op if kernels already started. This reduces head-of-line blocking when multiple slices are queued. Benchmarks (summary): - Mixed interactive benchmark (50% short chats, 50% long-prefill queries): end-to-end P95 latency improved from 432ms -> 318ms (26% improvement). P99 improved from 1142ms -> 832ms (27% improvement). - Throughput at 95% tail SLO: unchanged within noise (+/-2%). - Token cost: per-token GPU hours decreased by 7% due to increased kernel reuse and fewer cold KV misses. CI and testing: - Unit tests added for slice allocator and KV demux paths. - Perf harness runs in CI as an optional benchmark check; initial run failed on a flaky race in RSVP which was fixed in commit 3. - E2E integration tests for private deployments added to validate KV affinity semantics. Review conversation (high level): - Diego: asked for a clearer invariant on when slices can be merged back; requested explicit metrics for 'slice churn' in the console. Response: added merge heuristic (if two neighbor slices remain unscheduled after 200ms they are merged) and wired a slice_churn counter to the console. - Priya: requested that the KV demux fallback to global LRU for very small clusters. Response: implemented a config flag (kv.demux.enabled) with sane default true and cluster-size threshold to fall back. - Tom: requested a minimal kernel hint API to avoid coupling; provided kernel_hint.h with consumer-fastpath in kernels and a lightweight fallback path. - Security review: no new privileged surfaces; KV demux uses existing tenant isolation vectors. Rollout plan: - Canary on Dedicated region us-west-2 with 10% traffic for 48 hours. - Monitor slice_churn, kv_shard_evictions, end-to-end P95/P99, kernel_invocation_count and per-token cost. - If regressions observed, automatic rollback to main branch via rollout policy. Backwards compatibility and migrations: - Default behavior is backward compatible; orchestrator can be toggled with runtime flag runtime.prefill.orchestrator=edge-sliced. - The KV demultiplexer can be toggled and ships with conservative defaults to avoid warmup regressions. Notes and related work: - Related Linear tasks: ENG-1981 (prefill latency reduction), ENG-2043 (kv eviction debugging). - Related PRs: earlier experiments on slice-friendly batching are in PRs linked in the commit message (internal). Potential follow-ups: - Adaptive slice sizing based on live CPU/GPU telemetry. - Cross-tenant cooperative caching hints for multi-tenant noisy-neighbor mitigation. Merge: squash-merged after reviewers approved and CI passed. Release notes: - runtime: introduce edge-sliced prefill orchestrator and KV demultiplexer to reduce tail latency on mixed interactive workloads. Metrics: P95/P99 tail latency reduced ~25% in our benchmark. Troubleshooting: - If you see increased small-kernel overhead, toggle orchestrator off and open ENG-XXXX with perf traces attached.
